### Penanganan Keluhan Nasabah [F 24][2-25][2-26][413-1]

Sebagai bagian dari komitmen kami untuk memberikan layanan terbaik bagi nasabah, Permata Bank memiliki Divisi Service Excellence. Divisi ini terdiri dari Contact Center (PermataTel) yang melayani kebutuhan informasi, permintaan, dan keluhan nasabah dan non-nasabah, termasuk masyarakat, melalui telepon, surel, dan media sosial, serta Customer Care Center (CCC) yang fokus pada survei kepuasan nasabah dan penyelesaian kebutuhan dan keluhan nasabah dan non-nasabah secara cepat dan tepat.

Pada November 2024, Permata Bank turut serta menjadi bagian 20 bank yang berpartisipasi dalam menjalankan program OJK yang meluncurkan kanal pengaduan nasabah atas pelaporan transaksi terindikasi penipuan melalui situs web Indonesia Anti Scam Center (IASC), sehingga laporan dapat ditindaklanjuti dengan cepat.

Berdasarkan Service Level Agreement (SLA), keluhan nasabah harus diselesaikan dalam 10 hari kerja dan dapat diperpanjang 10 hari kerja bila dibutuhkan. Apabila melebihi batas waktu, Bank akan memberikan Surat Perpanjangan Jangka Waktu Penyelesaian kepada nasabah. Nasabah memiliki hak untuk mengajukan keberatan, jika merasa solusi yang diberikan belum sesuai. Nasabah dapat memilih untuk mengajukan keluhan ulang atau menggunakan jalur penyelesaian melalui dua pilihan External Dispute Resolution (EDR) yang sebagai berikut:

- Fasilitasi/mediasi perbankan (terbatas) oleh OJK;
- Penyelesaian di luar pengadilan, yaitu melalui Lembaga Alternatif Penyelesaian Sengketa Perbankan Sektor Jasa Keuangan (LAPS SJK).

### Customer Complaint Handling [F 24][2-25][2-26][413-1]

As part of its commitment to providing excellent service, Permata Bank has established the Service Excellence Division. This division comprises the Contact Center (PermataTel), which addresses information requests, customer and non-customer inquiries, and complaints via phone, e-mail, and social media, and the Customer Care Center (CCC), which focuses on customer satisfaction surveys and the efficient resolution of customer and non-customer needs and complaints.

In November 2024, Permata Bank participated in an OJK initiative involving 20 banks to launch a customer complaint channel for reporting suspected fraudulent transactions through the Indonesia Anti Scam Center (IASC) website, enabling swift follow-up on reports.

Under the Service Level Agreement (SLA), customer complaints must be resolved within 10 business days, with an extension of an additional 10 business days if necessary. If resolution exceeds this timeframe, the Bank provides a Time Extension Letter to the customer. Customers who are dissatisfied with the proposed solution may object by either submitting a new complaint or utilizing one of two External Dispute Resolution (EDR) mechanisms:

- Facilitation/limited banking mediation provided by OJK;
- Out-of-court resolution through the Financial Services Sector Banking Alternative Dispute Resolution Institution (LAPS SJK).

CERITA bertujuan untuk meningkatkan budaya dan kesadaran untuk menabung dengan menyebarkan pengetahuan terkait uang dan bank, serta pentingnya pelestarian lingkungan. Program ini dilaksanakan sekaligus sebagai bentuk dukungan Permata Bank terhadap program-program regulator, yaitu program tahunan Bulan Inklusi Keuangan (BIK) dan Gerakan Nasional Cerdas Keuangan (GENCARKAN) yang diinisiasi OJK. Tahun 2024 ini, BIK mengangkat tema “Akses Keuangan Inklusif, Wujudkan Masyarakat Produktif”. CERITA juga diadakan untuk mendukung Program Ayo Menabung yang dicanangkan oleh Bank Indonesia, serta dalam rangka rangka memperingati hari lahir Permata Bank pada akhir September.

Kegiatan CERITA dihadiri secara langsung oleh Direksi, perwakilan pejabat Permata Bank, serta perwakilan dari pihak OJK, Bank Indonesia, Kemendikbudristek, dan pemerintah daerah. Selain kegiatan literasi keuangan bagi siswa, Permata Bank juga memberikan bantuan prasarana sekolah seperti perbaikan kelas, sarana olahraga, perpustakaan, fasilitas lain di area sekolah, alat bantu ajar, serta bantuan untuk lingkungan di area sekolah, seperti penanaman apotek hidup, penanaman pohon, dan penyediaan tempat sampah. Kegiatan CERITA diselenggarakan pada tanggal 24-25 Oktober 2024 di 23 kantor cabang dengan melibatkan 631 EVO dan 2.288 siswa dan guru penerima manfaat.

As recognition, EVOs earn Smile Points based on their activities. Accumulated Smile Points are converted annually, with every 15 points providing one educational scholarship for an underprivileged child.

## 4. Permata CERITA (Cinta dan Edukasi daRI kiTA)

Permata CERITA is Permata Hati's flagship program, conducted simultaneously across several branches in Indonesia to provide financial literacy education to school-aged students (from kindergarten to high school, including Special-Needs Schools/SLB). The program engages hundreds of Employee Volunteers (EVOs) as key drivers.

![img-71.jpeg](img-71.jpeg)

CERITA aims to foster a culture and awareness of saving by sharing knowledge about money, banking, and the importance of environmental preservation. The program also supports regulatory initiatives such as the annual Financial Inclusion Month (BIK) and the National Financial Literacy Movement (GENCARKAN), initiated by OJK. In 2024, BIK adopted the theme "Inclusive Financial Access for a Productive Society". CERITA also aligns with Bank Indonesia's Ayo Menabung campaign and commemorates Permata Bank's anniversary in late September.

The CERITA activities were attended in person by the Board of Directors, Permata Bank officials, and representatives from OJK, Bank Indonesia, the Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology (Kemendikbudristek), and local governments. In addition to financial literacy sessions for students, Permata Bank provided support to schools, such as classroom renovations, sports facilities, libraries, teaching tools, and environmental contributions, including planting medicinal gardens, tree planting, and waste bin installations. The CERITA program was held on 24-25 October 2024, across 23 branch offices, involving 631 EVOs and benefiting 2,288 students and teachers.

Program ini bertujuan untuk konservasi Gajah Sumatra dengan menciptakan dan memperpanjang kehidupan ekosistem yang sehat, melalui cara menghargai, melindungi, dan mengatur sistem dan proses yang natural sebagai solusi terkait menjawab tantangan-tantangan di sosial, lingkungan, dan ekonomi. Melalui program ini, diharapkan alam Bukit Tigapuluh yang juga dihuni oleh masyarakat Suku Talang Mamak dan Suku Rimba ini tetap lestari dan berkelanjutan.

# Elephant Conservation Program in Bukit Tigapuluh, Jambi [8.2] [F.10][304-3]

In support of the national agenda outlined in the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and in response to climate change concerns, Permata Bank has taken concrete action by collaborating with WWF-Indonesia, a foundation dedicated to wildlife conservation, environmental protection, and biodiversity preservation for the well-being of present and future generations. This partnership led to the launch of the #DenganHati for Bukit Tigapuluh program, an initiative focused on the conservation of social and environmental ecosystems in Bukit Tigapuluh, Dusun Simerantihan, Suo-Suo Village, Tebo Regency, Jambi Province.

This program aims to protect the Sumatran elephant by fostering and extending the life of a healthy ecosystem through a holistic approach that respects, safeguards, and regulates natural systems and processes. By addressing social, environmental, and economic challenges, the program seeks to ensure the long-term sustainability of Bukit Tigapuluh, which is also home to the Suku Talang Mamak and Suku Rimba.

# 3 FOKUS AREA PROGRAM #DENGANHATI UNTUK BUKIT TIGAPULUH

3 Focus Areas of the #DenganHati for Bukit Tigapuluh Program

Kegiatan ini sejalan dengan komitmen untuk memberikan kontribusi melalui pelaksanaan program-program Tanggung Jawab Sosial dan Lingkungan yang berfokus pada:

1.  **Reforestasi**
Sebagai bagian dari upaya pemulihan lahan untuk melestarikan koridor habitat pajah, Bank melakukan penanaman hutan kembali dengan menanam bibit tanaman bernilai ekonomis di area hutan yang gundul seluas 8 ha dan total luasan habitat yang dilindungi dengan status konsesi restorasi ekosistem.

2.  **Mewujudkan Kemandirian Ekonomi bagi Masyarakat**
a.  **Budidaya lebah kelulut**: Bank memfasilitasi 30 stup lebah untuk menghasilkan madu kelulut berkualitas dan meningkatkan keuntungan para petani. Pada tahun 2024, madu kelulut telah dipanen sebanyak 4,1 kg.
b.  **Budidaya tanaman bernilai ekonomi**: Bank berupaya memenuhi kebutuhan penghijauan kembali area tipis hutan melalui penanaman kayu-kayuan (gaharu), kopi, Multi-Purpose Tree Species (MPTS) seperti durian, matoa, mangga, alpukat, duku, dan buah-buahan lainnya, serta kelukup sebagai Non-Timber Forest Product (NTFP). Melalui penanaman ini, diharapkan dapat memberdayakan dan meningkatkan pendapatan masyarakat setempat, yaitu Suku Talang Mamak dan Suku Rimba.
c.  **Penyediaan fasilitas produksi**: Bank mengadakan penunjang alat produksi bagi petani perkebunan, antara lain pengadaan mesin kompos dan mesin pembelah jambe/pinang, serta pembangunan rumah jemur dan gudang pupuk.

3.  **Renovasi Fasilitas Pendidikan**
a.  **Renovasi fasilitas pendidikan**: Bank melakukan renovasi bangunan SDN 167-VIII Kelas Jauh Dusun Simerantihan yang hanya memiliki dua ruang kelas dengan total 48 anak didik. Pada tahun 2024, renovasi sekolah telah selesai dilaksanakan.
b.  **Literasi edukasi keuangan**: Bank akan memberikan pengajaran literasi keuangan dasar dengan menggunakan modul keuangan dasar dan pembelajaran melalui simulasi permainan.

This initiative aligns with the Bank's commitment to contributing through Social and Environmental Responsibilities programs, focusing on:

1.  **Reforestation**
As part of land restoration efforts to preserve the elephant habitat corridor, the Bank has undertaken reforestation by planting economically valuable tree seedlings across 8 hectares of deforested land, within the total protected habitat area with ecosystem restoration concession status.

2.  **Realizing Economic Independence for Local Communities**
a.  **Stingless bee farming**: The Bank facilitated 30 bee hives to produce high-quality stingless bee honey (madu kelulut), increasing farmers' earnings. In 2024, a total of 4.1 kg of madu kelulut was harvested.
b.  **Cultivation of economically valuable plants**: The Bank also promotes the cultivation of economically valuable plants to support forest regeneration in degraded areas. This includes planting agarwood (gaharu), coffee, Multi-Purpose Tree Species (MPTS) such as durian, matoa, mango, avocado, duku, and other fruits, as well as kelukup as a Non-Timber Forest Product (NTFP). These reforestation efforts aim to empower and increase the income of local communities, particularly the Suku Talang Mamak and Suku Rimba.
c.  **Provision of production facilities**: The Bank supplies essential farming equipment, including composting machines and areca nut splitting machine, and constructed drying houses and fertilizer storage facilities to support plantation farmers.

3.  **Renovation of Educational Facilities**
a.  **Renovation of educational facilities**: The Bank renovated SDN 167-VIII Kelas Jauh Dusun Simerantihan, which previously had only two classrooms serving 48 students. The renovation was completed in 2024.
b.  **Financial education literacy**: The Bank will provide basic financial literacy training using fundamental financial education modules and interactive learning through simulation games.

# Tata Kelola Keberlanjutan [2-9][2-12][2-13]

## Sustainability Governance

Sehubungan dengan penerapan POJK No. 17 Tahun 2023 tentang Penerapan Tata Kelola bagi Bank Umum, Permata Bank melakukan beberapa penyesuaian kebijakan dan prosedur sebagai wujud kepatuhan dan juga upaya memperkuat tata kelola yang mengedepankan prinsip keterbukaan, akuntabilitas, tanggung jawab, independensi, dan kewajaran, dengan mengintegrasikan aspek keberlanjutan. Selain POJK No. 17/2023, Permata Bank juga melaksanakan tata kelola dengan mengadopsi standar internasional ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard (ACGS) 2023, best practice, serta peraturan lainnya yang berlaku.

Setiap tahunnya, Bank telah melaksanakan self-assessment untuk memastikan kepatuhan Bank terhadap regulasi yang berlaku serta penerapan Tata Kelola Perusahaan yang Baik (GCG). Hasil rekomendasi self-assessment telah diterapkan oleh Direksi dan Dewan Komisaris. [2-11]

Permata Bank menyadari dari pemberian kredit, secara langsung maupun tidak langsung juga terpapar risiko lingkungan, termasuk kerusakan hutan, hilangnya keanekaragaman hayati, kerusakan lingkungan laut dan sumber air, serta risiko sosial seperti pelanggaran hak asasi manusia dan hak-hak tenaga kerja. Oleh sebab itu, untuk memperkuat fungsi Keberlanjutan di tahun 2024, terdapat penyesuaian struktur organisasi dengan memindahkan Departemen Keberlanjutan ke dalam Divisi Corporate Secretary & Sustainability serta penyesuaian pada Terms of Reference (TOR) dan keanggotaan pada Komite Keberlanjutan.

Komite Keberlanjutan terdiri dari anggota tetap dengan hak suara yaitu Direktur Utama, Direktur Risiko, dan Direktur Keuangan, serta anggota tetap tanpa hak suara yang berasal dari Chief dan Kepala Divisi yang terkait seperti Corporate Banking, Commercial Banking, International Business Development & Advisory, Treasury, Corporate Secretary & Sustainability, Corporate Communication, dan Consumer Lending. Komite Keberlanjutan dapat mengundang Kepala Divisi Permata Bank lainnya berdasarkan topik yang akan didiskusikan di rapat.

Komite Keberlanjutan bertanggung jawab untuk mengawasi dan mempromosikan inisiatif keberlanjutan di Permata Bank; mengintegrasikan aspek LST ke dalam strategi, kebijakan, dan praktik bisnis Bank; serta memastikan kepatuhan Bank terhadap peraturan yang berlaku, kesesuaian standar industri dan praktik umum terkait keberlanjutan di perbankan.

In line with the implementation of Financial Services Authority Regulation (POJK) No. 17 of 2023 concerning the Governance Implementation for Commercial Banks, Permata Bank has undertaken several improvements on policies and procedures as a form of compliance and an effort to improve the principles of transparency, accountability, responsibility, independency, and fairness while at the same time integrating sustainability aspects. In addition to POJK No. 17/2023, Permata Bank has adopted the 2023 ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard (ACGS) international standards, best practices, and other applicable regulations.

Each year, the Bank conducts a self-assessment to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and the implementation of Good Corporate Governance (GCG). The recommendations from the self-assessment have been implemented by the Board of Directors along with the Board of Commissioners. [2-11]

Permata Bank is aware that by providing credit, it is directly or indirectly exposed to environmental risks, including forest destruction, loss of biodiversity, damage to the marine environment and water sources, as well as social risks such as violations of human rights and labor rights. To strengthen the Sustainability function in 2024, adjustments were made to the organizational structure, including relocating the Sustainability Department into the Corporate Secretary & Sustainability Division and revising the Terms of Reference (TOR) as well as membership of the Sustainability Committee.

The Sustainability Committee comprises permanent members with voting rights: the President Director, the Risk Director, and the Finance Director. Additionally, the Committee has non-voting permanent members from Chiefs and Division Heads of relevant divisions such as Corporate Banking, Commercial Banking, International Business Development & Advisory, Treasury, Corporate Secretary & Sustainability, Corporate Communication, and Consumer Lending. The Sustainability Committee may also invite other Division Heads of Permata Bank to attend meetings based on the topics to be discussed.

The Sustainability Committee is responsible for overseeing and promoting Permata Bank's sustainability initiatives; integrating ESG aspects thoroughly into the Bank's strategies, policies, and business practices; and ensuring the Bank's compliance with relevant regulations, industry standards, and general practices related to sustainability in the banking sector.

# Manajemen Risiko [E3]

## Risk Management

Permata Bank melakukan pengelolaan semua tipe risiko material yang telah teridentifikasi dengan berpedoman pada Enterprise Risk Management Framework (ERMF). Proses manajemen risiko mencakup identifikasi, pengukuran, pemantauan, dan pengendalian kegiatan operasional Bank sebagai upaya meminimalisasi dampak negatif risiko terhadap ekonomi, sosial, lingkungan, dan tata kelola. Strategi manajemen risiko dirancang untuk jangka panjang dengan tujuan menghasilkan keuntungan dan memberikan nilai tambah kepada seluruh pemangku kepentingan dengan mempertimbangkan faktor internal dan eksternal.

Sesuai Enterprise Risk Management Framework (ERMF) 2024, Permata Bank mengelola 15 tipe risiko utama, yaitu Risiko Kredit, Risiko Pasar, Risiko Likuiditas Jangka Pendek, Risiko Likuiditas Struktural, Risiko Modal, Risiko Operasional, Risiko Keamanan Informasi, Risiko Hukum, Risiko Strategik, Risiko Kepatuhan, Risiko Imbal Hasil, Risiko Investasi, Risiko Transaksi Intra-group, dan termasuk Risiko Iklim. Permata Bank juga telah menyusun kajian manajemen risiko yang mencakup seluruh aspek operasional Bank, termasuk risiko terkait LST dan ekonomi. Risiko dan peluang bisnis utama terkait aspek LST akan dipantau dan dinilai dalam Komite Keberlanjutan yang diadakan minimal dua kali setahun.

Permata Bank telah mengidentifikasi dampak Risiko Iklim terhadap strategi bisnis dalam jangka pendek, menengah, dan panjang serta menentukan Risiko Iklim yang material dengan menggunakan analisis skenario dan uji stres. Dampak Risiko Iklim yang berhasil diidentifikasi mencakup dua kategori utama, yaitu Risiko Transisi dan Risiko Fisik. Risiko Transisi berkaitan dengan perubahan kebijakan, perubahan teknologi, perubahan preferensi sosial. Sementara Risiko Fisik meliputi banjir dan kebakaran.

Dampak Risiko Iklim dipetakan terhadap Risiko Keuangan dan Non-Keuangan untuk menilai potensi, signifikansi, dan konsentrasinya. Pengkajian atas risiko terkait iklim juga dilakukan selama proses onboarding debitur, aplikasi kredit dan tinjauan kredit, pemantauan dan keterlibatan berkelanjutan dengan debitur, serta persetujuan produk atau bisnis baru. Permata Bank juga melakukan komunikasi aktif dengan debitur dan pihak ketiga yang dianggap signifikan (seperti pemasok barang) untuk memperoleh informasi yang lebih baik mengenai pemahaman terhadap Risiko Iklim, rekam jejak, komitmen, serta strategi transisi dalam mengelola risiko tersebut.

Permata Bank manages all identified material risk types by adhering to the Enterprise Risk Management Framework (ERMF). The risk management process encompasses the identification, measurement, monitoring, and control of the Bank's operational activities to minimize the negative impact of risks on economic, social, environmental, and governance aspects. The risk management strategy is designed with a long-term perspective to generate profits and create added value for all stakeholders by considering both internal and external factors.

In line with the 2024 Enterprise Risk Management Framework (ERMF), Permata Bank manages 15 primary types of risk: Credit Risk, Market Risk, Short-Term Liquidity Risk, Structural Liquidity Risk, Capital Risk, Operational Risk, Information Security Risk, Legal Risk, Strategic Risk, Compliance Risk, Yield Risk, Investment Risk, Intra-Group Transaction Risk, and Climate Risk. Additionally, Permata Bank has developed a comprehensive risk management study addressing all aspects of the Bank's operations, including ESG and economic risks. Key business risks and opportunities related to ESG aspects are monitored and assessed within the Sustainability Committee, which convenes at least twice a year.

Permata Bank has identified the impact of Climate Risk on its business strategies over the short, medium, and long terms using scenario analysis and stress testing. The identified Climate Risk fall into two primary categories: Transition Risk and Physical Risk. Transition Risk relates to policy changes, technological advancements, and shifting social preferences. Meanwhile, Physical Risk include floods and wildfires.

The impact of Climate Risk is mapped to Financial and Non-Financial Risks to assess their potential, significance, and concentration. Assessments of climate-related risks are also conducted during the onboarding process for debtors, credit application reviews, credit monitoring, and the approval of new products or businesses. Permata Bank actively communicates with significant debtors and third parties (such as key suppliers) to obtain better insights into their understanding of Climate Risks, track records, commitments, and transition strategies for managing these risks.

Informasi lebih lengkap mengenai pelaksanaan serta peran dan tanggung jawab Direksi dan Dewan Komisaris dalam manajemen risiko secara keseluruhan dapat dilihat dalam Bab Manajemen Risiko Laporan Tahunan Permata Bank Tahun 2024.

Further information on the roles and responsibilities of the Board of Directors and the Board of Commissioners regarding overall risk management can be viewed in Management Risk Chapter in Permata Bank's 2024 Annual Report.

# Pengelolaan Risiko Iklim [2-13][FN-CB-550a.2]

Pengelolaan Risiko Iklim di Permata Bank dilakukan di bawah pengawasan Direktur Risiko selaku Risk Framework Owner (RFO) dari Risiko Iklim, yang dalam aktivitas kesehariannya didukung oleh RFO PIC yang terdiri dari Division Head Market and Enterprise Management (MERM), Division Head Corporate Commercial & Emerging Business Banking Credit Risk Management (CCE CRM), serta Division Head Corporate Secretary & Sustainability. Sejalan dengan penambahan Risiko Iklim sebagai risiko utama, Permata Bank juga telah membentuk Kerangka Kerja Tipe Risiko Iklim (Climate Risk Type Framework) serta menerapkan Taksonomi Hijau Indonesia (THI) yang kemudian diperkuat menjadi Taksonomi untuk Keuangan Berkelanjutan Indonesia (TKBI) untuk memastikan penerapan prinsip keuangan berkelanjutan yang efektif dan mengatasi isu-isu terkait iklim. Departemen Climate Risk Analytics juga telah dibentuk pada tahun 2024 di bawah Divisi MERM dengan fokus pada pengembangan Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) dan perhitungan Financed Emission.

Pada tahun 2024, Permata Bank telah melakukan CRST pertama kalinya sesuai dengan persyaratan regulasi dan telah disetujui oleh Direktur Risiko dan Direktur Keuangan & Unit Usaha Syariah, serta disajikan kepada Komite Pemantau Risiko (KPR) dan Komite Manajemen Risiko (KMR) untuk memberikan update mengenai identifikasi risiko dan dampaknya kepada Direksi dan Dewan Komisaris. Hasil CRST dapat digunakan sebagai pertimbangan pengambilan pengambilan keputusan maupun penerapan strategi keberlanjutan.

Frekuensi pelaksanaan CRST akan sejalan dengan persyaratan regulasi, mengingat regulasi Risiko Iklim adalah dokumen yang terus berkembang. Pendekatan yang dilakukan CSRT telah mengikuti panduan OJK dengan menerapkan skenario-skenario yang ditentukan (Net Zero 2050, Delay Transition, Current Policy) terhadap Risiko Transisi dan Risiko Fisik.

Secara garis besar, debitur diklasifikasikan ke dalam sub-sektor prioritas yang telah ditentukan tingkat risikonya (High, Medium, dan Low), kemudian dilakukan uji ketahanan atas debitur, baik untuk jangka pendek (2024-2026) maupun jangka panjang (2030-2050). Uji ketahanan dilakukan dengan melihat dampak skenario terhadap perubahan Credit Risk Grading (CRG) debitur dan dampak finansial terhadap Permata Bank secara keseluruhan melalui proyeksi Loan Impairment (LI), Risk Weighted Asset (RWA), dan Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR). Selain dampak pada Risiko Kredit, CRST secara umum juga diaplikasikan untuk mengukur dampak terhadap Risiko Pasar, Risiko Likuiditas, dan Risiko Operasional.

Melalui pilot bottom-up CRST di tahun 2024 terhadap 50% portofolio, Permata Bank mengidentifikasi dampak dari Risiko Transisi dan Risiko Fisik terhadap penurunan Profit After Tax (PAT) serta penurunan Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) dalam jangka pendek (2024-2026) menjadi sebesar 30%-31% dan dalam jangka panjang (2030-2050) menjadi sebesar 32%-33% dibandingkan Desember 2023 yang mencapai 38%. # Climate Risk Management [2-13][FN-CB-550a.2]

Climate Risk management at Permata Bank is overseen by the Risk Director as the Risk Framework Owner (RFO) for Climate Risk, supported in daily operations by RFO PICs, including the Division Head Market and Enterprise Management (MERM), Division Head Corporate Commercial & Emerging Business Banking Credit Risk Management (CCE CRM), and Division Head Corporate Secretary & Sustainability. By recognizing Climate Risk as a significant concern, Permata Bank has established a Climate Risk Type Framework and introduced the Indonesian Green Taxonomy (THI), which has been further strengthened into the Indonesian Sustainable Finance Taxonomy (TKBI) to ensure the effective implementation of sustainable finance principles and address climate-related issues. Additionally, the Climate Risk Analytics Department was established in 2024 under the MERM Division, focusing on the development of the Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) and the calculation of Financed Emissions.

In 2024, Permata Bank conducted its first CSRT in compliance with regulatory requirements, approved by the Risk Director and the Finance & Sharia Business Unit Director. The results were presented to the Risk Management Committee (RMC) and Risk Monitoring Committee (RMOC) to update the Board of Directors and the Board of Commissioners on risk identification and its impacts. The CRST results can be used as a consideration for decision-making and the implementation of the Bank's sustainability strategy.

The frequency of CRST implementation will align with regulatory requirements, as Climate Risk regulations are continuously evolving. The CRST approach adheres the OJK guidelines, applying specified scenarios (Net Zero 2050, Delay Transition, Current Policy) to assess Transition and Physical Risks.

In general, debtors are classified into priority sub-sectors based on their risk levels (High, Medium, and Low), followed by resilience testing for both the short term (2024-2026) and the long term (2030-2050). Resilience testing evaluates the impact of scenarios on changes in debtor Credit Risk Grading (CRG) and financial impacts on Permata Bank, including projections of Loan Impairment (LI), Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA), and Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR). Beyond Credit Risk, CRST is also applied to measure impacts on Market Risk, Liquidity Risk, and Operational Risk.

Through a pilot bottom-up CRST conducted in 2024 covering 50% of its portfolio, Permata Bank identified the impacts of Transition and Physical Risks on the decline in Profit After Tax (PAT) and the Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR). In the short term (2024-2026), these declined to 30%-31%, and in the long term (2030-2050) to 32%-33%, compared to December 2023 levels of 38%. ## Compliance with Laws and Regulations [2-27]

Permata Bank has Compliance Policy in place where the compliance function is overseen by the Legal and Compliance Director, supported by several divisions, including Compliance Regulatory Affairs Advisory, Compliance Monitoring & Training, Anti-Money Laundering (AML), and Cross-Border Compliance Advisory. To promote compliance awareness and implementation across all organizational levels, Permata Bank conducts mandatory annual compliance culture training (e-learning) for all employees. The Litigation Division also regularly holds legal sharing sessions for employees to raise awareness of prudential banking practices, ensuring consistent adherence to applicable regulations, including laws, guidelines, and internal procedures.

1. 2. Conducting periodic reviews of the Bank's policies and procedures to ensure alignment with the Document Governance Policy and Document Governance Guidelines Procedure.

## Issues in Sustainable Finance Implementation

Sejak penerapan keuangan berkelanjutan di tahun 2019, Permata Bank menghadapi berbagai tantangan akibat perkembangan peraturan dan persyaratan, serta perubahan kondisi ekonomi, sosial, dan lingkungan. Pada tahun 2024, tantangan yang harus dihadapi oleh Bank, di antaranya:

- Peningkatan jumlah transaksi digital dapat meningkatkan risiko keamanan data (information security) Bank dan nasabah;
- Pemahaman terhadap pengertian dan implementasi prinsip keuangan berkelanjutan maupun LST, baik untuk karyawan ataupun nasabah masih belum merata;
- Pemahaman mengenai dokumen-dokumen lingkungan terkait persyaratan pemberian kredit serta pemahaman mengenai Risiko Iklim yang perlu ditingkatkan secara internal; dan

- The increasing volume of digital transactions, which heightens the risk of data security (information security) for the Bank and its customers;
- Uneven understanding and implementation of sustainable finance and ESG principles among employees and customers;
- The need to enhance internal understanding of environmental documentation requirements for credit approval and Climate Risk awareness; and

## Challenges and Progress in Implementing Sustainable Governance

Komitmen Indonesia terhadap Enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution (E-NDC) yang meningkatkan target pengurangan emisi hingga 31,89% dengan upaya nasional dan 43,20% dengan dukungan internasional pada tahun 2030, menandai langkah besar dalam mitigasi perubahan iklim. Komitmen ini mendorong seluruh industri, termasuk industri jasa keuangan, untuk berperan aktif dalam pengelolaan Risiko Iklim.

Sejalan dengan komitmen ini, Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK) melalui POJK No. 17/2023 mendorong perbankan untuk memperkuat tata kelola yang baik dalam mengelola risiko terkait iklim. Regulasi ini mengharuskan bank untuk menilai potensi dampak terkait iklim; menghitung risiko terkait iklim; menetapkan peran dan tanggung jawab Dewan Komisaris, Direksi, dan unit kerja dalam pengelolaan risiko terkait iklim; memiliki kebijakan, prosedur, dan pengendalian untuk manajemen risiko terkait iklim.

Indonesia's commitment to the Enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution (E-NDC) which increases the emission reduction target to 31.89% through national efforts and 43.20% with international support by 2030, marks a significant step in climate change mitigation. This commitment calls for all industries, including the financial services industry, to play an active role in managing Climate Risks.

In line with this commitment, the Financial Services Authority (OJK) through POJK No. 17/2023, encourages the banking sector to strengthen good governance in managing climate-related risks. This regulation mandates banks to assess the potential impacts of climate change; calculate climate-related risks; define roles and responsibilities of the Board of Commissioners, the Board of Directors, and relevant work units in managing these risks; and establish policies, procedures, and controls for climate risk management.

# Adherence to AA1000AP (2018) and GRI Universal Standards

**Inclusivity** – The Bank has implemented inclusivity principles through structured engagement mechanisms, such as annual general meetings, public disclosures, employee town halls, vendor socialization sessions, and regulatory compliance reporting. The Bank’s stakeholder engagement activities are implemented by taking into account the diverse perspectives of customers, employees, regulators, vendors, and local communities. The Bank has also integrated inclusivity by conducting employee well-being programs, financial inclusion initiatives, sustainable business training for vendors, and anti-corruption compliance sessions. Through continuous dialogue via digital platforms and social medias, the Bank ensures that stakeholder feedback is acknowledged.

**Materiality** – The Bank has implemented a structured approach to identifying and prioritizing material topics for its sustainability reporting, which includes a Focus Group Discussion (FGD) and input from key governance bodies, ensuring that material topics align with the Bank’s performance results and stakeholder expectations. Material topics were identified based on insights from Board of Directors interviews and considerations. However, involving external stakeholders, such as customers and investors, in the materiality assessment process would provide a broader perspective and enhance the relevance of selected topics.

**Responsiveness** – The Bank has established mechanisms for addressing stakeholder concerns, including grievance procedures for employees and customer complaint resolution systems. The Bank manages employee grievances through discussions with supervisors and formal channels such as the Whistleblowing System (WBS) to ensure transparency and fairness. For customer complaints, the Bank follows a Service Level Agreement (SLA) to resolve issues in a timely manner and has integrated digital platforms for efficient complaint handling. While the Bank has demonstrated a commitment to addressing stakeholder concerns, improvements could be made by disclosing the progress made in response to customer complaints to show how concerns are addressed.

**Impact** – The Bank has realized its commitment to sustainability through various initiatives that generate impacts. The Bank conducted financial literacy programs in its effort to enhance financial management skills among students and underserved communities, supporting broader economic empowerment. The Bank has a zero data privacy breach as a result of its data security governance and compliance with personal data protection regulations. In environmental aspect, the Bank has increased its green financing. In social aspects, the Bank has conducted various initiatives, including entrepreneurship training for persons with disabilities, empowerment for small and medium enterprises, and conservation projects, and contribution to social and environmental benefits.
